statement: Combined FY2027 capex of the 5 largest AI/cloud spenders >= 1.2x FY2026 (securities filings; on FY2027 filings)
status_at_phase_end: Not resolvable until FY2027 filings; 2024 shows the trajectory. The four largest Bloc A cloud/platform spenders raised capex every quarter of 2024: ~$104B in H1 (+47% y/y) and ~$59-65B in Q3 alone (+56-68% y/y depending on lease treatment); full-year 2024 ~$230B. All four signalled further increases for 2025 ('significant' growth per one CFO). Growth far exceeded the 1.2x bar; the 2024 base also set a high comparison level. Q4 2024 figures were published only in 2025 and are excluded.

items.summary: In Q4 2023 results, one large Bloc A platform guided 2024 capex of $30-37B and others signalled notably larger 2024 AI infrastructure spending than 2023.
items.detail: Meta Q4 2023 earnings (2024-02-01), SEC Form 8-K Exhibit 99.1: 'We anticipate our full-year 2024 capital expenditures will be in the range of $30-37 billion' (checked 2026-11-19 in the web.archive.org copy; the investor-site press release URL now returns 404). Alphabet (2024-01-30) said 2024 capex 'notably larger' than 2023.

items.summary: First-half 2024 combined capex of the four largest Bloc A spenders ~$104B (+47% y/y). Q2: one firm $13.2B (+91% y/y), another $8.5B (+33%); a third raised the low end of its 2024 guidance to $37B.
items.detail: I/O Fund via Forbes (2024-08-08 and 2024-11-14); Meta Q2 2024 (2024-07-31, CNBC/NYT): capex $8.47B, guidance $37-40B; Alphabet Q2 $13.2B. Figures include finance-lease principal for some firms.

items.summary: A Bloc A cloud provider, an asset manager and a Gulf state-backed investor launched an AI-infrastructure partnership targeting $30B of equity and up to $100B including debt for data centres and power.
items.detail: Global AI Infrastructure Investment Partnership (BlackRock, GIP, Microsoft, MGX), announced 2024-09-17. Not verified via web_extract this run; announced intent, not filings.

items.summary: Q3 2024 combined capex of the four: ~$58.9B (+59% y/y) on cash P&E, ~$64.9B (+68% y/y) including finance leases; one firm said quarterly spending would hold ~$13B in Q4 with a further increase in 2025, another raised its 2024 range to $38-40B and expects 'significant' 2025 growth; a third expected ~$75B for 2024.
items.detail: S&P Global Market Intelligence (Nov 2024): $58.86B vs $36.95B a year earlier; I/O Fund via Forbes 2024-11-14: $64.9B. Meta Q3 2024 results (8-K Exhibit 99.1, 2024-10-30): capex incl. finance-lease principal $9.20B, 2024 guide $38-40B. Alphabet Q3 call (2024-10-29). Amazon Q3 (2024-10-31): ~$75B 2024.

items.summary: Analyst tracking: big-tech capex ~$170B through Q3 2024 (+56% y/y) and projected to exceed a quarter-trillion dollars in 2025.
items.detail: Forbes / I/O Fund 'AI Spending To Exceed A Quarter Trillion Next Year' (2024-11-14). Dell'Oro estimated the four increased data-centre infrastructure investment 81% y/y in Q3 (Construction Dive).

items.summary: Spender list and capex definition are not fixed (cash P&E vs including finance leases; fiscal years ending June; fifth spender undetermined). Same gap as later phases.
items.detail: Differences of ~$6B/quarter in 2024 between S&P (cash) and I/O Fund (incl. leases) totals illustrate the definitional sensitivity.
